# 🎛️ ResonanceFX **A free and open-source audio effects suite for rooted Android** — a hardened DSP engine, a universal root module, and a modern Material You app. No ads, no tracking, no network. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-v2.2.1-8b9dd8?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX/releases/latest) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-5.0%2B-3ddc84?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX) [![Root managers](https://img.shields.io/badge/Magisk%20·%20KernelSU%20·%20APatch-supported?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX)
## ✨ Highlights - 🎚️ **28 effect modules** — 10-band equalizer (56 presets), 15/31-band graphic EQ, parametric EQ (up to 32 bands), AutoEQ (thousands of headphones), loudness compensation (ISO 226, follows the volume), multiband compressor, dynamic EQ, de-esser, vocals & ambience (centre extraction), spatial audio (MIT KEMAR HRTF, head tracking on Android 13+), convolver (impulse responses, auto-resampled to the live output rate), headphone correction (`.vdc` profiles), FET compressor, playback gain control, bass and clarity enhancers, field/differential surround, headphone surround, reverb, dynamic system (103 headphone profiles), tube simulator, analog coloration, crossfeed, output gain/balance/limiter. - 🔊 **Made for speakers too** — speaker correction (phone, tablet, laptop, Bluetooth, car and TV profiles), 🎤 **measure your own speaker** with the phone's microphone and get a correction fitted to it, speaker protection (an excursion limiter that holds back bass a small driver can't play, or limited at each band's measured distortion point) and speaker widening (crosstalk cancellation for closely spaced speakers, following how the device is held). - 📐 **Measured, not claimed** — every effect's measured response, distortion and loudness change ships in the app and with each release. - 💾 **Per-device profiles** that switch automatically for speaker, wired, every Bluetooth device and USB DAC; JSON presets with import/export. - 📡 **Live status** — see whether the engine is registered, attached and processing, with a built-in test tone and a copyable diagnostics report. The status screens read a snapshot published by the foreground service: zero effect-handle polling from the UI. - 🛡️ **Robust engine** — any channel layout (1–28 ch), PCM 16/24/32-bit, 8.24 and float, saturating output (no wrap-around crackle), real-time-safe locking, bounds-checked commands; arm, arm64, x86, x86_64, 16 KB pages; dithered 16-bit output. - 🔄 **Self-healing** — re-attaches after audioserver restarts, re-uploads impulse responses when the output sample rate changes, and quietly backs off its own health probes when your audio is paused (nothing to heal, nothing to disturb). - 🔒 **Private** — no ads, no analytics, no network permission. The microphone is only used when you measure a speaker, and the recording never leaves memory. ## 📥 Install Download both files from the [latest release](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX/releases/latest). 1. 🧩 Flash `ResonanceFX-.zip` in Magisk, KernelSU or APatch and reboot. 2. 📲 Install `ResonanceFX.apk`, open it and turn effects on. 3. ✅ The **Status** tab confirms: engine registered → attached → stream accepted → processing. If the engine doesn't load, tap the module's **Action** button in your root manager: it re-patches every config, re-applies mounts, restarts the audio services and prints what it found. Logs: `/data/adb/resonancefx/logs/` (`install.log`, `boot.log`, `logcat.txt`, `action.log`). After every boot the module description shows a ✅/⚠️/❌ verdict, confirmed against the audio HAL's list of registered effects. ## ⚙️ How the module loads reliably - 🔍 Finds every `audio_effects*.xml|.conf` (HIDL, AIDL `audio_effects_config.xml`, SKU variants, vendor-specific names) on `/odm`, `/vendor`, `/system_ext`, `/product`, `/my_product`, `/mi_ext` (and `/system` on Android 7 and older), and adds the effect to all of them: which files a HAL loads is vendor-specific. - ♻️ Re-generates the patched copies from the *current* stock files on every boot, so OTA updates never leave stale configs. - 🧼 Patching is idempotent and tolerant: removes stale entries, handles inline and self-closing ``, ignores commented-out tags, reuses the soundfx path in legacy `.conf` files. - 🏔️ Uses the root manager's own overlay first, verifies after mounting and bind-mounts only what's missing, with SELinux labels copied from the originals — and never stacks a second bind on a node still holding one. - 🧬 Installs the 32-bit engine too when the device has 32-bit userspace (many 64-bit phones still run a 32-bit audio HAL). - 🛌 Skips mount work entirely in recovery sessions, where nothing should be patched. ## 🛠️ Build Requirements: Android SDK with NDK 27+, CMake 3.22+, JDK 21; Linux/WSL g++ for engine tests. ```sh scripts/build-engine.sh # out/engine//libresonancefx.so scripts/build-module.sh # out/ResonanceFX-.zip (cd app && ./gradlew assembleRelease) # app/app/build/outputs/apk/release/ tests/test-patch.sh # config patcher (add "busybox sh" to run under busybox) tests/run-engine-tests.sh # engine through AELI with ASan/UBSan (Linux/WSL) tests/measure-engine.sh # per-effect measurements (Linux/WSL) tests/emulator-test.sh # end to end on a rooted emulator/device over adb (cd app && ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug) ``` Release APKs are signed with the key given in `RFX_KEYSTORE`, `RFX_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `RFX_KEY_ALIAS` and `RFX_KEY_PASSWORD`; without them the debug key is used. Pushing a `v*` tag builds the module and app on GitHub Actions and publishes a release (see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#-releases)). ## 🗂️ Layout - `engine/` — engine (`src/android/` effect glue, `src/core/` DSP core, `src/fx/` effects), `engine/tests/` host harness - `module/` — root module scripts (`common.sh` holds all logic) - `app/` — Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) - `docs/` — licensing notes - `.github/` — CI, release workflow, issue templates - `tests/` — patcher fixtures and test runners ## 📄 License GPL-3.0-or-later. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) for third-party data attributions, and [`docs/LICENSING.md`](docs/LICENSING.md) for how the engine was written.

🎛️ ResonanceFX

A free and open-source audio effects suite for rooted Android — a hardened DSP engine,

a universal root module, and a modern Material You app. No ads, no tracking, no network.

![Release](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX/releases/latest)

![License](LICENSE)

![Android](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX)

![Root managers](https://github.com/xeloria/ResonanceFX)

✨ Highlights

  • 🎚️ **28 effect modules** — 10-band equalizer (56 presets), 15/31-band graphic EQ, parametric

    • EQ (up to 32 bands), AutoEQ (thousands of headphones), loudness compensation (ISO 226,

    follows the volume), multiband compressor, dynamic EQ, de-esser, vocals & ambience (centre

    extraction), spatial audio (MIT KEMAR HRTF, head tracking on Android 13+), convolver (impulse

    responses, auto-resampled to the live output rate), headphone correction (.vdc profiles),

    FET compressor, playback gain control, bass and clarity enhancers, field/differential

    surround, headphone surround, reverb, dynamic system (103 headphone profiles), tube

    simulator, analog coloration, crossfeed, output gain/balance/limiter.

  • 🔊 **Made for speakers too** — speaker correction (phone, tablet, laptop, Bluetooth, car and

    • TV profiles), 🎤 measure your own speaker with the phone's microphone and get a

    correction fitted to it, speaker protection (an excursion limiter that holds back bass a

    small driver can't play, or limited at each band's measured distortion point) and speaker

    widening (crosstalk cancellation for closely spaced speakers, following how the device is

    held).

  • 📐 **Measured, not claimed** — every effect's measured response, distortion and loudness

    • change ships in the app and with each release.

  • 💾 **Per-device profiles** that switch automatically for speaker, wired, every Bluetooth

    • device and USB DAC; JSON presets with import/export.

  • 📡 **Live status** — see whether the engine is registered, attached and processing, with a

    • built-in test tone and a copyable diagnostics report. The status screens read a snapshot

    published by the foreground service: zero effect-handle polling from the UI.

  • 🛡️ **Robust engine** — any channel layout (1–28 ch), PCM 16/24/32-bit, 8.24 and float,

    • saturating output (no wrap-around crackle), real-time-safe locking, bounds-checked

    commands; arm, arm64, x86, x86_64, 16 KB pages; dithered 16-bit output.

  • 🔄 **Self-healing** — re-attaches after audioserver restarts, re-uploads impulse responses

    • when the output sample rate changes, and quietly backs off its own health probes when your

    audio is paused (nothing to heal, nothing to disturb).

  • 🔒 **Private** — no ads, no analytics, no network permission. The microphone is only used

    • when you measure a speaker, and the recording never leaves memory.

    📥 Install

    Download both files from the latest release.

  • 🧩 Flash `ResonanceFX-.zip` in Magisk, KernelSU or APatch and reboot.
  • 📲 Install `ResonanceFX.apk`, open it and turn effects on.
  • ✅ The **Status** tab confirms: engine registered → attached → stream accepted → processing.

    • If the engine doesn't load, tap the module's Action button in your root manager: it

    re-patches every config, re-applies mounts, restarts the audio services and prints what it

    found. Logs: /data/adb/resonancefx/logs/ (install.log, boot.log, logcat.txt,

    action.log). After every boot the module description shows a ✅/⚠️/❌ verdict, confirmed

    against the audio HAL's list of registered effects.

    ⚙️ How the module loads reliably

  • 🔍 Finds every `audio_effects*.xml|.conf` (HIDL, AIDL `audio_effects_config.xml`, SKU

    • variants, vendor-specific names) on /odm, /vendor, /system_ext, /product,

    /my_product, /mi_ext (and /system on Android 7 and older), and adds the effect to all

    of them: which files a HAL loads is vendor-specific.

  • ♻️ Re-generates the patched copies from the *current* stock files on every boot, so OTA

    • updates never leave stale configs.

  • 🧼 Patching is idempotent and tolerant: removes stale entries, handles inline and

    • self-closing , ignores commented-out tags, reuses the soundfx path in legacy

    .conf files.

  • 🏔️ Uses the root manager's own overlay first, verifies after mounting and bind-mounts only

    • what's missing, with SELinux labels copied from the originals — and never stacks a second

    bind on a node still holding one.

  • 🧬 Installs the 32-bit engine too when the device has 32-bit userspace (many 64-bit phones

    • still run a 32-bit audio HAL).

  • 🛌 Skips mount work entirely in recovery sessions, where nothing should be patched.

    • 🛠️ Build

    Requirements: Android SDK with NDK 27+, CMake 3.22+, JDK 21; Linux/WSL g++ for engine tests.

    scripts/build-engine.sh                  # out/engine/<abi>/libresonancefx.so
scripts/build-module.sh                  # out/ResonanceFX-<version>.zip
(cd app && ./gradlew assembleRelease)    # app/app/build/outputs/apk/release/

tests/test-patch.sh                      # config patcher (add "busybox sh" to run under busybox)
tests/run-engine-tests.sh                # engine through AELI with ASan/UBSan (Linux/WSL)
tests/measure-engine.sh                  # per-effect measurements (Linux/WSL)
tests/emulator-test.sh                   # end to end on a rooted emulator/device over adb
(cd app && ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug)

    Release APKs are signed with the key given in RFX_KEYSTORE, RFX_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD,

    RFX_KEY_ALIAS and RFX_KEY_PASSWORD; without them the debug key is used. Pushing a v* tag

    builds the module and app on GitHub Actions and publishes a release (see

    CONTRIBUTING.md).

    🗂️ Layout

  • `engine/` — engine (`src/android/` effect glue, `src/core/` DSP core, `src/fx/` effects),

    • engine/tests/ host harness

  • `module/` — root module scripts (`common.sh` holds all logic)
  • `app/` — Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose)
  • `docs/` — licensing notes
  • `.github/` — CI, release workflow, issue templates
  • `tests/` — patcher fixtures and test runners

    • 📄 License

    GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE, NOTICE for third-party data

    attributions, and docs/LICENSING.md for how the engine was written.
